Apple (AAPL) Shares Bought by Personal Capital Advisors Corp Posted by Dante Gardener | Apr 19th, 2018 
Personal Capital Advisors Corp raised its holdings in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 5.4% in the fourth quarter, according to its most recent 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The firm owned 293,308 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after purchasing an additional 15,122 shares during the quarter. Apple accounts for 0.8% of Personal Capital Advisors Corp’s investment portfolio, making the stock its 19th largest position. Personal Capital Advisors Corp’s holdings in Apple were worth $49,636,000 as of its most recent SEC filing. 
A number of other large investors have also made changes to their positions in AAPL. New Capital Management LP raised its holdings in shares of Apple by 24.4% in the 4th quarter. New Capital Management LP now owns 21,618 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $3,229,000 after acquiring an additional 4,234 shares in the last quarter. Moller Financial Services purchased a new position in shares of Apple during the 4th quarter valued at about $553,000. Cibc Bank USA raised its holdings in shares of Apple by 2.4% during the 4th quarter. Cibc Bank USA now owns 60,567 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $10,250,000 after buying an additional 1,414 shares in the last quarter. Naples Global Advisors LLC increased its stake in Apple by 5.3% in the 4th quarter. Naples Global Advisors LLC now owns 38,606 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $6,533,000 after purchasing an additional 1,948 shares during the period. Finally, Baker Boyer National Bank increased its stake in Apple by 1.5% in the 4th quarter. Baker Boyer National Bank now owns 31,591 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,346,000 after purchasing an additional 453 shares during the period. Hedge funds and other institutional investors own 61.35% of the company’s stock. 
NASDAQ AAPL opened at $177.84 on Thursday. The stock has a market capitalization of $904,392.13, a PE ratio of 19.31, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.35 and a beta of 1.25. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a current ratio of 1.24 and a quick ratio of 1.20. Apple has a twelve month low of $140.45 and a twelve month high of $183.50. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its quarterly earnings data on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share for the quarter, topping analysts’ consensus estimates of $3.82 by $0.07. The firm had revenue of $88.29 billion during the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $87.62 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 37.37% and a net margin of 21.13%. The business’s quarterly revenue was up 12.7% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same quarter in the prior year, the company posted $3.36 earnings per share. equities research analysts predict that Apple will post 11.37 earnings per share for the current fiscal year. 
In other news, insider Luca Maestri sold 39,122 shares of the stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, April 13th. The stock was sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total value of $6,833,048.52. Following the sale, the insider now directly owns 64,475 shares in the company, valued at $11,261,203.50. The sale was disclosed in a document filed with the SEC, which is available at this link . Also, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the stock in a transaction that occurred on Tuesday, April 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total value of $11,564,692.22. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last three months, insiders have sold 125,988 shares of company stock valued at $21,336,201. 0.08% of the stock is owned by corporate insiders. 
A number of equities analysts have commented on AAPL shares. BMO Capital Markets reaffirmed a “buy” rating and issued a $199.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research note on Wednesday, December 20th. Loop Capital reaffirmed a “buy” rating and issued a $200.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research note on Friday, December 22nd. Rosenblatt Securities set a $180.00 price target on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Tuesday, December 26th. Wells Fargo reaffirmed a “hold” rating and issued a $195.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research note on Wednesday, December 27th. Finally, ValuEngine raised Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a research note on Sunday, December 31st. Two equities research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have given a hold rating, thirty-two have assigned a buy rating and one has assigned a strong buy rating to the stock. The stock currently has an average rating of “Buy” and an average price target of $203.21.
